1 رَصُنَ , (S, M, K,) inf. n. رَصَانَةٌ, (S, M,) It (a thing, M, or a building, TA) was, or became, firm, stable, strong, solid, compact, or sound. (S, M, * K. *) ―
-b2- Also, said of a man, i. q. رَزُنَ (assumed tropical:) [He was, or became, grave, staid, steady, sedate, or calm; and forbearing: still, or motionless: or firm, or sound, of judgment: wise, or sensible]. (M.) ＝
-A2- رَصَنَهُ, (As, S, M, K,) aor.
رَصُنَ , inf. n. رَصَنٌ, (As, S,) He made it complete, entire, or perfect; (As, S, M, K;) namely, a thing. (As, S.) ―
-b2- See also 4. ―
-b3- And see 2, in two places. ―
-b4- رَصَنَهُ بِلِسَانِهِ, (S, K,) inf. n. رَصْنٌ, (S,) He reviled him, or vilified him. (S, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
